decision_reason: NASA publishes the Input Device Framework as a reusable product, its current NASA catalog entry links to the exact public repo, NASA's 2024 training podcast describes its operational use to connect varied physical controls, and the repo remains actively developed. The exact framework grant is NOSA 1.3; the NASA Trick third-party submodule retains its own separate terms.

government_provenance.note: NASA's official catalog identifies and distributes the exact Input Device Framework as an open-source NASA product. The repository's NASA-maintained README describes its architecture and scope; NASA's 2024 podcast gives current first-party examples of use with astronaut and study-group controls.

public_source.note: Public repository contains the IDF library, applications/examples, build configuration, docs, and tests without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact license states NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3, an OSI-approved grant (https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3). The bundled Trick submodule is separately licensed.

primary_evidence.note: A NASA podcast describes using the exact input device framework to connect almost any physical control for astronauts and study groups. The NASA catalog provides an official product record and download; the repository wiki is linked for installation guidance.

decision_reason: NASA Glenn publishes the exact IPv6 Python Extension Module as an open-source NASA product; the source provides a versioned release, installation/use examples, and a specialized API for IPv6 flow-label manipulation. primary_evidence.note: The live NASA catalog page names the exact module, describes its flow-label function, marks it Open Source, and links to the assigned repository. The repo's release 1.23 page and README give supported Python versions, installation, and usage.

decision_reason: The source is a real NASA Glenn lab inventory application with Apache-2.0 app source, but the README says it was created for one lab to track roughly 350 assets, and I found no versioned release, agency-wide distribution, independent reuse, current exact deployment/support evidence, or user documentation beyond local developer setup. It fails the baseline's notability/current-product gate; an internally scoped app in the NASA org is not itself an agency reusable product.

government_provenance.note: The README explicitly says one NASA Glenn Research Center lab requested a tool to track its own equipment and that the application was developed for that need.
